title.en: Volume 37 Biographies 18: Dao Hui, Liu Quan, Yu Cong, Hu Xiezhi

sentences.zh: 到撝

translations.literal: Dao Hui
translations.idiomatic: Dao Hui

sentences.zh: 到撝字茂謙，彭城武原人也。

translations.literal: Dao Hui, styled Maoqian, was a native of Wuyuan in Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Dao Hui, styled Maoqian, was a man of Wuyuan in Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 祖彥之，宋驃騎將軍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yanzhi was Song General of Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yanzhi had been Song General of Agile Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 父仲度，驃騎從事中郎。

translations.literal: His father Zhongdu was Attendant Gentleman of the General of Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhongdu had served as Attendant Gentleman on the staff of the General of Agile Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 撝襲爵建昌公。

translations.literal: Hui inherited the title Duke of Jianchang.
translations.idiomatic: Hui inherited the title of Duke of Jianchang.

sentences.zh: 起家爲太學博士，除奉車都尉，試守延陵令，非所樂，去官。

translations.literal: He began his career as an Erudite of the Imperial Academy, was appointed Commandant of the Chariots for the Imperial Household, and was tried as acting magistrate of Yanling, which he did not enjoy, so he left office.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as an Erudite of the Imperial Academy, was appointed Commandant of the Chariots for the Imperial Household, and served a trial term as magistrate of Yanling; finding the post uncongenial, he resigned.

sentences.zh: 除新安王北中郎行參軍，坐公事免。

translations.literal: He was appointed acting staff officer on the Prince of Xin'an's Northern Gentlemen-in-Attendance staff, and was dismissed for an official matter.
translations.idiomatic: He was made acting staff officer on the Prince of Xin'an's Northern Gentlemen-in-Attendance staff, but was dismissed over an official offense.

sentences.zh: 除新安王撫軍參軍，未拜，新安王子鸞被殺，仍除長兼尚書左民郎中。

translations.literal: He was appointed staff officer on the Prince of Xin'an's Pacification Army, but before he took up the post Prince Ziluan of Xin'an was killed; he was then appointed acting concurrent Director of the Left Bureau for the People in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed staff officer on the Prince of Xin'an's Pacification Army, but before he could take up the post Prince Ziluan of Xin'an was killed; he was then made acting concurrent Director of the Left Bureau for the People in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 明帝立，欲收物情，以撝功臣後，擢爲太子洗馬。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming acceded, wishing to win popular sentiment, because Hui was descended from a meritorious minister he was promoted to Groom of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming came to the throne, wishing to win hearts, he promoted Hui—descended from a meritorious minister—to Groom of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 除王景文安南諮議參軍。

translations.literal: He was appointed advisory staff officer on Wang Jingwen's Pacification of the South staff.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed advisory staff officer on Wang Jingwen's Pacification of the South staff.

sentences.zh: 撝資籍豪富，厚自奉養，宅宇山池，京師第一，妓妾姿藝，皆窮上品。

translations.literal: Hui's family background was extravagantly wealthy; he lavished care on himself, and his residence with its hills and pools was first in the capital; his singing girls and concubines in beauty and talent were all of the highest grade.
translations.idiomatic: Hui came from a fabulously wealthy family and lived in lavish style; his mansion with its gardens and ponds was unrivaled in the capital, and his courtesans and concubines in looks and talent were all of the finest rank.

sentences.zh: 才調流贍，善納交遊，庖廚豐腆，多致賔客。

translations.literal: His talent and manner were fluent and generous; he was skilled at cultivating friendships, his kitchens were rich and abundant, and he drew many guests.
translations.idiomatic: Gifted and open-handed, he was adept at winning friends; his kitchens were lavish, and he entertained a large circle of guests.

sentences.zh: 愛妓陳玉珠，明帝遣求，不與，逼奪之，撝頗怨望。

translations.literal: He loved his courtesan Chen Yuzhu; Emperor Ming sent to request her, and he would not give her up, so she was seized by force, and Hui was deeply resentful.
translations.idiomatic: He doted on his courtesan Chen Yuzhu; when Emperor Ming sent to demand her, he refused to surrender her, and after she was taken by force he nursed a deep grievance.

sentences.zh: 帝令有司誣奏撝罪，付廷尉，將殺之。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the relevant offices to lodge a false accusation of Hui's crimes and hand him to the Minister of Justice, intending to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the authorities to frame charges against Hui and hand him over to the Minister of Justice, intending to have him put to death.

sentences.zh: 撝入獄，數宿鬚鬢皆白。

translations.literal: Hui entered prison, and within several nights his beard and temples turned white.
translations.idiomatic: After Hui entered prison, within a few nights his beard and temples had turned white.

sentences.zh: 免死，繫尚方，奪封與弟賁。

translations.literal: He was spared death, detained in the Imperial Workshops, and his enfeoffment was taken away and given to his younger brother Ben.
translations.idiomatic: He was spared execution but held in the Imperial Workshops, and his noble title was stripped and given to his younger brother Ben.

sentences.zh: 撝由是屏斥聲玩，更以貶素自立。

translations.literal: Hui thereupon set aside music and diversions and instead established himself through plain austerity.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Hui renounced music and worldly pleasures and made a point of living plainly and frugally.

sentences.zh: 帝除撝爲羊希恭寧朔府參軍，徙劉韞輔國、王景文鎮南參軍，竝辭疾不就。

translations.literal: The emperor appointed Hui staff officer on Yang Xigong's Pacification of the North staff, then transferred him to staff posts on Liu Yun's Army That Assists the State and Wang Jingwen's Army That Guards the South, but in each case he pleaded illness and did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor appointed Hui staff officer on Yang Xigong's Pacification of the North staff, then moved him to posts on Liu Yun's Army That Assists the State and Wang Jingwen's Army That Guards the South, but each time he pleaded illness and declined.

sentences.zh: 尋板假明威將軍，仍除桂陽王征南參軍，轉通直郎，解職。

translations.literal: Soon he was provisionally granted the title General of Illustrious Might, then appointed staff officer on the Prince of Guiyang's Southern Expedition staff, transferred to Attendant of Direct Communication, and resigned.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was provisionally made General of Illustrious Might, then appointed staff officer on the Prince of Guiyang's Southern Expedition staff, transferred to Attendant of Direct Communication, and left office.

sentences.zh: 帝崩後，弟賁表讓封還撝，朝議許之。

translations.literal: After the emperor died, his younger brother Ben memorialized to yield the enfeoffment back to Hui, and court deliberation approved it.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor's death, his younger brother Ben petitioned to return the title to Hui, and the court approved.

sentences.zh: 遷司徒左西屬，又不拜。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Western Subordinate of the Left on the Minister of Education's staff, and again did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Western Subordinate of the Left on the Minister of Education's staff, but again declined the appointment.

sentences.zh: 居家累年。

translations.literal: He remained at home for many years.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in retirement at home for many years.

sentences.zh: 弟遁，元徽中爲寧遠將軍、輔國長史、南海太守，在廣州。

translations.literal: His younger brother Dun, in the Yuanhui era was General of Pacifying the Distance, Chief Clerk of the Army That Assists the State, and Grand Administrator of Nanhai, stationed in Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Dun, during the Yuanhui era, served as General of Pacifying the Distance, Chief Clerk of the Army That Assists the State, and Grand Administrator of Nanhai, and was posted at Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: ，沈攸之反，刺史陳顯達起兵以應朝廷，遁以猶預見殺。

translations.literal: When Shen Youzhi rebelled, the inspector Chen Xianda raised troops in response to the court, and Dun was killed for prior involvement.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen Youzhi rebelled, Inspector Chen Xianda raised troops in support of the court, and Dun was executed for his earlier complicity.

sentences.zh: 遁家人在都，從野夜歸，見兩三人持堊刷其家門，須臾滅，明日而遁死問至。

translations.literal: Dun's family in the capital, returning from the countryside at night, saw two or three men whitewashing their gate; in a moment they vanished, and the next day news of Dun's death arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Dun's family in the capital, returning from the countryside one night, saw two or three men whitewashing their gate; the figures vanished in an instant, and the next day word of Dun's death arrived.

sentences.zh: 撝遑懼，詣太祖謝，卽板爲世祖中軍諮議參軍。

translations.literal: Hui was fearful and alarmed, went to the Founding Emperor to apologize, and was immediately provisionally appointed advisory staff officer on the Heir Apparent's Central Army staff.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Hui went to the Founding Emperor to apologize and was at once provisionally appointed advisory staff officer on the future Emperor Wu's Central Army staff.

sentences.zh: 建元初，遷司徒右長史，出爲永嘉太守，爲黃門郎，解職。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyuan he was transferred to Senior Clerk of the Right on the Minister of Education's staff, went out as Grand Administrator of Yongjia, became Gentleman at the Yellow Gates, and resigned.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jianyuan era he was made Senior Clerk of the Right on the Minister of Education's staff, then served as Grand Administrator of Yongjia, became Gentleman at the Yellow Gates, and left office.

sentences.zh: 世祖卽位，遷太子中庶子，不拜。

translations.literal: When the Heir Apparent acceded, Hui was transferred to Household Subordinate of the Heir Apparent, but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu came to the throne, Hui was promoted to Household Subordinate of the Heir Apparent, but declined the post.

sentences.zh: 又除長沙王中軍長史，司徒左長史。

translations.literal: He was also appointed Senior Clerk on the Prince of Changsha's Central Army staff and Senior Clerk of the Left on the Minister of Education's staff.
translations.idiomatic: He was also appointed Senior Clerk on the Prince of Changsha's Central Army staff and Senior Clerk of the Left on the Minister of Education's staff.

sentences.zh: 宋世，上數遊會撝家，同從明帝射雉郊野，渴倦，撝得早青瓜，與上對剖食之。

translations.literal: In Song times the emperor often visited and feasted at Hui's home; together they followed Emperor Ming to shoot pheasants in the countryside, and when thirsty and weary Hui obtained an early green melon and split it with the emperor to eat.
translations.idiomatic: In Song times the emperor often visited Hui's home; once, while accompanying Emperor Ming to hunt pheasants in the countryside, they grew thirsty and tired, and Hui brought an early green melon and shared it with the emperor.

sentences.zh: 上懷其舊德，意眄良厚。

translations.literal: The emperor cherished his old kindness and regarded him with great favor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor remembered his old kindness and treated him with exceptional favor.

sentences.zh: 至是一歲三遷。

translations.literal: By then he had been promoted three times in one year.
translations.idiomatic: By then he had been promoted three times within a single year.

sentences.zh: ，加輔國將軍，轉御史中丞。

translations.literal: He was additionally made General Who Assists the State and transferred to Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made General Who Assists the State and transferred to Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 車駕幸丹陽郡宴飲，撝恃舊，酒後狎侮同列，言笑過度，爲左丞庾杲之所糾，贖論。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage visited Danyang commandery for a feast, Hui relied on their old ties; after wine he was familiar and insulting toward his colleagues, laughing and talking excessively, and was impeached by the Left Assistant Director Yu Gaozhi and sentenced to commutation by payment.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor visited Danyang commandery for a banquet, Hui presumed on their old friendship; drunk, he was overly familiar and insulting toward his colleagues and carried on beyond propriety, and was impeached by Left Assistant Director Yu Gaozhi and fined in lieu of punishment.

sentences.zh: 三年，復爲司徒左長史，轉左衞將軍。

translations.literal: In the third year he again became Senior Clerk of the Left on the Minister of Education's staff and was transferred to General of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he again became Senior Clerk of the Left on the Minister of Education's staff, then was transferred to General of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 隨王子隆帶彭城郡，撝問訊，不修民敬，爲有司所舉，免官。

translations.literal: Prince Zilong of Sui held Pengcheng commandery concurrently; Hui paid a courtesy call but did not observe the proper respect due the people, was reported by the relevant offices, and was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Zilong of Sui concurrently administered Pengcheng commandery, Hui paid a courtesy visit but failed to observe the required formalities; the authorities reported him, and he was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 久之，白衣兼御史中丞。

translations.literal: After a long while he served in plain clothes as concurrent Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he served in plain clothes as concurrent Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 轉臨川王驃騎長史，司徒左長史，遷五兵尚書，出爲輔國將軍、廬陵王中軍長史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Senior Clerk on the Prince of Linchuan's General of Agile Cavalry staff, then Senior Clerk of the Left on the Minister of Education's staff, promoted to Minister of the Five Weapons, and went out as General Who Assists the State and Senior Clerk on the Prince of Luling's Central Army staff.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Senior Clerk on the Prince of Linchuan's General of Agile Cavalry staff, then Senior Clerk of the Left on the Minister of Education's staff, promoted to Minister of the Five Weapons, and went out as General Who Assists the State and Senior Clerk on the Prince of Luling's Central Army staff.

sentences.zh: 母憂去官，服未終，八年，卒，年五十八。

translations.literal: He left office for his mother's mourning; before the mourning period ended, in the eighth year he died at age fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his mother; before the mourning period had ended, in the eighth year he died at the age of fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 弟賁，初爲衞尉主簿，奉車都尉。

translations.literal: His younger brother Ben, at first was Chief Clerk of the Minister of the Guards and Commandant of the Chariots for the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Ben first served as Chief Clerk of the Minister of the Guards and as Commandant of the Chariots for the Imperial Household.

sentences.zh: 昇明初，爲中書郎，太祖驃騎諮議。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shengming he was Gentleman of the Secretariat and advisory officer on the Founding Emperor's Rapid Cavalry staff.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Shengming era he was Gentleman of the Secretariat and advisory officer on the Founding Emperor's Rapid Cavalry staff.

sentences.zh: 建元中，爲征虜司馬，卒。

translations.literal: In the Jianyuan era he was Major on the Punitive Campaign against the Barbarians staff and died.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jianyuan era he served as Major on the Punitive Campaign against the Barbarians staff and died.

sentences.zh: 賁弟坦，解褐本州西曹。

translations.literal: Ben's younger brother Tan, upon leaving coarse cloth became Western Clerk of his home province.
translations.idiomatic: Ben's younger brother Tan, upon entering official life, became Western Clerk of his home province.

sentences.zh: ，亦爲太祖驃騎參軍。

translations.literal: He also served as staff officer on the Founding Emperor's Rapid Cavalry staff.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as staff officer on the Founding Emperor's Rapid Cavalry staff.

sentences.zh: 歷豫章王鎮西驃騎二府諮議。

translations.literal: He successively served as advisory officer on the Prince of Yuzhang's Army That Guards the West and General of Agile Cavalry staffs.
translations.idiomatic: He successively served as advisory officer on the staffs of the Prince of Yuzhang's Army That Guards the West and General of Agile Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 坦美鬚髯，與世祖豫章王有舊。

translations.literal: Tan had a handsome beard and whiskers and had old ties with the Heir Apparent, the Prince of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Tan had a fine beard and whiskers and was on old terms with the future Emperor Wu, then Prince of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 坦仍隨府轉司空太尉參軍。

translations.literal: Tan then followed the prince's staff and was transferred to staff officer posts on the Minister of Education and Grand Marshal staffs.
translations.idiomatic: Tan then followed the prince's household and was transferred to staff posts on the Minister of Education and Grand Marshal staffs.

sentences.zh: 出爲晉安內史，還又爲大司馬諮議，中書郎，卒。

translations.literal: He went out as Interior Secretary of Jin'an, returned and again became advisory officer on the Grand Marshal's staff and Gentleman of the Secretariat, then died.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as Interior Secretary of Jin'an, returned to court as advisory officer on the Grand Marshal's staff and Gentleman of the Secretariat, and died.

sentences.zh: 劉悛

translations.literal: Liu Quan
translations.idiomatic: Liu Quan

sentences.zh: 劉悛字士操，彭城安上里人也。

translations.literal: Liu Quan, styled Shicao, was a native of Anshang village in Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Quan, styled Shicao, was a man of Anshang village in Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 彭城劉同出楚元王，分爲三里，以別宋氏帝族。

translations.literal: The Liu of Pengcheng, like others, descended from the King Yuan of Chu and were divided into three villages to distinguish them from the Song imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: The Liu of Pengcheng, like other branches of the clan, traced their descent to King Yuan of Chu and were divided into three villages to distinguish them from the Song imperial house.

sentences.zh: 祖穎之，汝南新蔡二郡太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yingzhi was Grand Administrator of the two commanderies of Runan and Xincai.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yingzhi had been Grand Administrator of Runan and Xincai commanderies.

sentences.zh: 父勔，司空。

translations.literal: His father Kan was Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: His father Kan had served as Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 劉延孫爲南徐州，初辟悛從事，隨父勔征竟陵王誕於廣陵，以功拜駙馬都尉，轉宗愨寧蠻府主簿，建安王司徒騎兵參軍。

translations.literal: When Liu Yansun was governor of South Xuzhou he first recruited Quan as an aide; he followed his father Kan in campaigning against Prince Dan of Jingling at Guangling, and for merit was appointed Commandant of the Palace Stables, transferred to chief clerk on Zong Que's Pacification of the Barbarians staff, and staff cavalry officer on the Prince of Jian'an's Minister of Education staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yansun governed South Xuzhou he first recruited Quan as an aide; Quan followed his father Kan in the campaign against Prince Dan of Jingling at Guangling and, for his service, was appointed Commandant of the Palace Stables, then became chief clerk on Zong Que's Pacification of the Barbarians staff and cavalry staff officer on the Prince of Jian'an's Minister of Education staff.

sentences.zh: 復隨父勔征殷琰於壽春，於橫塘、死虎累戰皆勝。

translations.literal: He again followed his father Kan in campaigning against Yin Yan at Shouchun, and in repeated battles at Hengtang and Sihu all were victories.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed his father Kan in the campaign against Yin Yan at Shouchun and fought repeated victorious battles at Hengtang and Sihu.

sentences.zh: 歷遷員外郎，太尉司徒二府參軍，代世祖爲尚書庫部郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted through appointments as External Clerk, staff officer on the Grand Marshal and Minister of Education staffs, and replaced the Heir Apparent as Director of the Treasury Bureau in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the posts of External Clerk and staff officer on the Grand Marshal and Minister of Education staffs, and replaced the future Emperor Wu as Director of the Treasury Bureau in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 遷振武將軍、蜀郡太守，未之任，復從父勔征討，假寧朔將軍，拜鄱陽縣侯世子。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General Who Exerts Martial Might and Grand Administrator of Shujun, did not take up the post, again followed his father Kan on campaign, was provisionally made General of Pacifying the North, and was appointed heir to the Marquis of Poyang county.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General Who Exerts Martial Might and Grand Administrator of Shujun but did not take up the post; he again followed his father Kan on campaign, was provisionally made General of Pacifying the North, and was named heir to the Marquis of Poyang.

sentences.zh: 轉桂陽王征北中兵參軍，與世祖同直殿內，爲明帝所親待，由是與世祖款好。

translations.literal: He was transferred to central army staff officer on the Prince of Guiyang's Northern Expedition staff, served on palace duty together with the Heir Apparent, was personally favored by Emperor Ming, and thereby became intimate friends with the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to central army staff officer on the Prince of Guiyang's Northern Expedition staff, served on palace duty alongside the future Emperor Wu, won Emperor Ming's personal favor, and thereby became close friends with the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 遷通直散騎侍郎，出爲安遠護軍、武陵內史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attendant Cavalier of Direct Communication, and went out as Protector of Pacifying the Distance and Interior Secretary of Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Attendant Cavalier of Direct Communication and went out as Protector of Pacifying the Distance and Interior Secretary of Wuling.

sentences.zh: 郡南江古堤，久廢不緝。

translations.literal: In the commandery the ancient embankment on the southern Jiang had long been abandoned and unrepaired.
translations.idiomatic: In the commandery the ancient embankment on the southern Yangzi had long lain in disrepair.

sentences.zh: 悛脩治未畢，而江水忽至，百姓棄役奔走，悛親率厲之，於是乃立。

translations.literal: Quan had not finished the repairs when the river waters suddenly came; the people abandoned their labor and fled, but Quan personally led and urged them on, and thereby the work was completed.
translations.idiomatic: Before Quan had finished the repairs the river suddenly rose; the people abandoned their work and fled, but Quan personally rallied them, and the embankment was completed.

sentences.zh: 漢壽人邵榮興六世同爨，表其門閭。

translations.literal: Shao Rongxing of Hanshou had six generations eating from the same hearth; Quan memorialized to honor his gate and lane.
translations.idiomatic: Shao Rongxing of Hanshou had six generations living under one roof; Quan memorialized to honor his household.

sentences.zh: 悛強濟有世調，善於流俗。

translations.literal: Quan was forceful and resourceful with the tone of his generation and skilled in dealing with common custom.
translations.idiomatic: Quan was forceful and resourceful, with the bearing of his generation, and adept at winning popular favor.

sentences.zh: 蠻王田僮在山中，年垂百餘歲，南譙王義宣爲荊州，僮出謁。

translations.literal: The barbarian king Tian Tong lived in the mountains, nearly a hundred years old; when the Prince of Nanqiao Yixuan was governor of Jingzhou, Tong came out to pay his respects.
translations.idiomatic: The Man chieftain Tian Tong lived in the mountains, nearly a hundred years old; when Prince Yixuan of Nanqiao governed Jingzhou, Tong came out to pay his respects.

sentences.zh: 至是又出謁悛。

translations.literal: At this time he again came out to pay respects to Quan.
translations.idiomatic: Now he came out again to pay his respects to Quan.

sentences.zh: 明帝崩，表奔赴，敕帶郡還都。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming died, Quan memorialized to hurry to the capital; he was ordered to retain his commandery post and return to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming died, Quan petitioned to rush to the capital and was ordered to return while retaining his commandery post.

sentences.zh: 吏民送者數千人，悛人人執手，係以涕泣，百姓感之，贈送甚厚。

translations.literal: Several thousand officials and commoners came to see him off; Quan took each person's hand and wept with them; the people were moved and sent him off with very generous gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Several thousand officials and commoners came to see him off; Quan took each by the hand and wept with them; deeply moved, the people sent him away with lavish parting gifts.

sentences.zh: 仍除散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: He was then appointed Attendant Cavalier.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed Attendant Cavalier.

sentences.zh: 桂陽難，加寧朔將軍，助守石頭。

translations.literal: During the Guiyang crisis he was additionally made General of Pacifying the North and assisted in defending Stone City.
translations.idiomatic: During the Guiyang crisis he was additionally made General of Pacifying the North and helped defend Stone City.

sentences.zh: 父勔於大桁戰死，悛時疾病，扶伏路次，號哭求勔屍。

translations.literal: His father Kan died in battle at the Great Beam; Quan was then ill, but supported himself along the roadside, wailing and seeking Kan's corpse.
translations.idiomatic: His father Kan was killed in battle at the Great Beam; though ill, Quan dragged himself along the roadside, wailing and searching for his father's body.

sentences.zh: 勔屍項後傷缺，悛割髮補之。

translations.literal: Behind the neck on Kan's corpse there was a wound with missing flesh; Quan cut his hair to patch it.
translations.idiomatic: A piece of flesh was missing from the back of Kan's neck; Quan cut his own hair to fill the wound.

sentences.zh: 持喪墓側，冬月不衣絮。

translations.literal: He kept mourning beside the tomb and in winter months wore no padded garments.
translations.idiomatic: He kept vigil at the tomb and, even in winter, wore no padded clothing.

sentences.zh: 太祖代勔爲領軍，素與勔善，書譬悛曰：「承至性毀瘵，轉之危慮，深以酸怛。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor replaced Kan as Commander of the Guards, had long been on good terms with Kan, and wrote to admonish Quan, saying: "I have learned of your utmost nature destroying your health and turning to perilous anxiety; I am deeply pained and distressed.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor, who replaced Kan as Commander of the Guards and had long been on good terms with him, wrote to admonish Quan: "I have heard how your utmost filial devotion is ruining your health and driving you toward danger, and I am deeply grieved.

sentences.zh: 終哀全生，先王明軌，豈有去縑纊，徹溫席，以此悲號，得終其孝性邪？

translations.literal: To complete mourning and preserve life is the enlightened king's clear standard—how can there be removing silk padding and withdrawing warm mats, and with such wailing hope to fulfill one's filial nature?"
translations.idiomatic: To finish mourning while preserving one's life is the enlightened kings' clear standard—how can you cast off padded silks and warm bedding and, by wailing in this way, hope to fulfill your filial duty?"

sentences.zh: 當深顧往旨，少自抑勉。」

translations.literal: "You should deeply consider past injunctions and restrain yourself somewhat."
translations.idiomatic: "You should take past injunctions deeply to heart and moderate yourself a little."

sentences.zh: 建平王景素反，太祖總衆軍出頓玄武湖。

translations.literal: Prince Jingsu of Jianping rebelled, and the Founding Emperor gathered the armies and encamped at Xuanwu Lake.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Jingsu of Jianping rebelled, the Founding Emperor gathered the armies and encamped at Xuanwu Lake.

sentences.zh: 悛初免喪，太祖欲使領支軍，召見悛兄弟，皆羸削改貌，於是乃止。

translations.literal: Quan had just ended mourning; the Founding Emperor wished to have him lead a separate army, but when he summoned Quan and his brothers they were all emaciated and altered in appearance, and so he desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Quan had just left mourning; the Founding Emperor wished to put him in command of a separate force, but when he summoned Quan and his brothers they were so wasted and changed in appearance that he abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 除中書郎，行宋南陽八王事，轉南陽王南中郎司馬、長沙內史，行湘州事。

translations.literal: He was appointed Gentleman of the Secretariat, acted in the affairs of the eight Song princes of Nanyang, was transferred to Major on the Prince of Nanyang's Southern Gentlemen-in-Attendance staff and Interior Secretary of Changsha, and acted in the affairs of Xiang province.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Gentleman of the Secretariat, handled the affairs of the eight Song princes of Nanyang, was transferred to Major on the Prince of Nanyang's Southern Gentlemen-in-Attendance staff and Interior Secretary of Changsha, and acted as governor of Xiang province.

sentences.zh: 未發，霸業初建，悛先致誠節。

translations.literal: Before he set out, as the founding enterprise was first being built, Quan was the first to offer his loyal devotion.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could depart, as the founding enterprise was taking shape, Quan was among the first to pledge his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 沈攸之事起，加輔國將軍。

translations.literal: When Shen Youzhi's affair arose, Quan was additionally made General Who Assists the State.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen Youzhi rebelled, Quan was additionally made General Who Assists the State.

sentences.zh: 世祖鎮盆城，上表西討，求悛自代。

translations.literal: The Heir Apparent was stationed at Pencheng; he memorialized to campaign west and asked that Quan replace him.
translations.idiomatic: When the future Emperor Wu was stationed at Pencheng, he memorialized to campaign west and asked that Quan replace him.

sentences.zh: 世祖旣不行，悛除黃門郎，行吳郡事。

translations.literal: Since the Heir Apparent did not go, Quan was appointed Gentleman at the Yellow Gates and acted in the affairs of Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When the Heir Apparent did not go west, Quan was appointed Gentleman at the Yellow Gates and acted as administrator of Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 尋轉晉熙王撫軍中軍二府長史，行揚州事。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Senior Clerk on the Prince of Jinxi's Pacification Army and Central Army staffs and acted in the affairs of Yang province.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to Senior Clerk on the Prince of Jinxi's Pacification Army and Central Army staffs and acted as governor of Yang province.

sentences.zh: 出爲持節、督廣州、廣州刺史，將軍如故。

translations.literal: He went out bearing the staff of authority as Supervisor of Guang province and Governor of Guangzhou, his general's title unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He went out bearing the staff of authority as Supervisor and Governor of Guang province, retaining his general's rank.

sentences.zh: 襲爵鄱陽縣侯。

translations.literal: He inherited the title Marquis of Poyang county.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the title of Marquis of Poyang.

sentences.zh: 世祖自尋陽還，遇悛於舟渚閒，歡宴敘舊，停十餘日乃下。

translations.literal: When the Heir Apparent returned from Xunyang he met Quan among the boat landings, feasted joyfully and recalled old times, and stayed more than ten days before disembarking.
translations.idiomatic: When the future Emperor Wu returned from Xunyang he met Quan at the boat landings; they feasted and reminisced, and stayed together more than ten days before parting.

sentences.zh: 遣文惠太子及竟陵王子良攝衣履，脩父友之敬。

translations.literal: He sent the Crown Prince Wenhuai and Prince Ziliang of Jingling to adjust their robes and shoes and pay the respect due a father's friend.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Crown Prince Wenhuai and Prince Ziliang of Jingling to straighten their dress and pay the respect due their father's old friend.

sentences.zh: 太祖受禪，國除。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor received the abdication, the state enfeoffment was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founding Emperor accepted the abdication, Quan's Song enfeoffment was abolished.

sentences.zh: 進號冠軍將軍。

translations.literal: His title was advanced to General Who Vanquishes the Foe.
translations.idiomatic: His rank was raised to General Who Vanquishes the Foe.

sentences.zh: 平西記室參軍夏侯恭叔上書，以柳元景中興功臣，劉勔殞身王事，宜存封爵。

translations.literal: Recorder of the Pacification of the West staff officer Xia Hougongshu memorialized that Liu Yuanjing was a meritorious minister of the restoration and Liu Kan gave his life in royal service, and their enfeoffments ought to be preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Hougongshu, recorder on the Pacification of the West staff, memorialized that Liu Yuanjing had been a meritorious minister of the restoration and Liu Kan had died in the state's service, and that their titles ought to be preserved.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「與運隆替，自古有之，朝議已定，不容復厝意也。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Rise and fall with the age have existed since antiquity; court deliberation is already settled and cannot again entertain such proposals.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "Rise and fall with the fortunes of the age have existed since antiquity; court deliberation is already settled, and such proposals cannot be entertained again.

sentences.zh: 」初，蒼梧廢，太祖集議中華門，見悛，謂之曰：「君昨直耶？

translations.literal: "At first, when Cangwu was deposed, the Founding Emperor gathered deliberation at the Zhonghua Gate, saw Quan, and said to him: "Were you upright yesterday?"
translations.idiomatic: "Earlier, when Emperor Cangwu was deposed, the Founding Emperor convened deliberation at the Zhonghua Gate, saw Quan, and asked him: "Were you upright yesterday?"

sentences.zh: 」悛答曰：「僕昨乃正直，而言急在外。

translations.literal: Quan answered: "Your servant yesterday was indeed upright, but my words were urgent and remain outside."
translations.idiomatic: Quan answered: "Your servant was indeed upright yesterday, but my words were urgent and remain unspoken."

sentences.zh: 」至是上謂悛曰：「功名之際，人所不忘。

translations.literal: At this time the emperor said to Quan: "At the juncture of merit and fame, people do not forget.
translations.idiomatic: Now the emperor said to Quan: "At the turning point of merit and fame, people do not forget.

sentences.zh: 卿昔於中華門答我，何其欲謝世事？

translations.literal: You once answered me at the Zhonghua Gate—how eager you were to withdraw from worldly affairs?"
translations.idiomatic: You once answered me at the Zhonghua Gate—how eager you were to withdraw from public life?"

sentences.zh: 」悛曰：「臣世受宋恩，門荷齊眷，非常之勳，非臣所及。

translations.literal: Quan said: "Your servant's family received Song grace for generations; our gate bears Qi favor—extraordinary merit is not something I can claim.
translations.idiomatic: Quan said: "My family received Song grace for generations; our house now bears Qi's favor—extraordinary merit is not mine to claim.

sentences.zh: 進不遠怨前代，退不孤負聖明，敢不以實仰答。」

translations.literal: Advancing I do not distance myself in resentment from the former dynasty; retreating I do not fail the sage clarity—how dare I not answer upward with truth?"
translations.idiomatic: In advancing I do not hold resentment toward the former dynasty; in retreat I do not fail your sage clarity—how could I answer you with anything but the truth?"

sentences.zh: 遷太子中庶子，領越騎校尉。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Household Subordinate of the Heir Apparent and concurrently Colonel of the Yue Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Household Subordinate of the Heir Apparent and concurrently Colonel of the Yue Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 時世祖在東宮，每幸悛坊，閑言至夕，賜屏風帷帳。

translations.literal: At that time the Heir Apparent was in the Eastern Palace; he often visited Quan's residence, conversed at leisure until evening, and bestowed screens and curtains.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the future Emperor Wu was in the Eastern Palace; he often visited Quan's home, talked until evening, and gave him screens and curtains.

sentences.zh: 世祖卽位，改領前軍將軍，中庶子如故。

translations.literal: When the Heir Apparent acceded he was changed to lead the Vanguard Army as general, his subordinate post unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu came to the throne, Quan was changed to command the Vanguard Army as general while retaining his post as Household Subordinate.

sentences.zh: 征北竟陵王子良帶南兖州，以悛爲長史，加冠軍將軍、廣陵太守。

translations.literal: Prince Ziliang of Jingling, General Who Conquers the North, concurrently held Southern Yan province; Quan was made Senior Clerk, and additionally appointed General Who Vanquishes the Foe and Administrator of Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ziliang of Jingling, General Who Conquers the North, also held Southern Yan province; he appointed Quan Senior Clerk and further made him General Who Vanquishes the Foe and Administrator of Guangling.

sentences.zh: 轉持節、都督司州諸軍事、司州刺史，將軍如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Bearer of the Staff, Supervisor of All Military Affairs in Si province, and Governor of Si province, his general's title unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Bearer of the Staff, overall commander of Si province, and Governor of Si, retaining his rank as general.

sentences.zh: 悛父勔討殷琰，平壽陽，無所犯害，百姓德之，爲立碑祀。

translations.literal: Quan's father Mou had campaigned against Yin Yan and pacified Shouyang, harming no one; the people thanked him and erected a stele in his honor.
translations.idiomatic: Quan's father Mou had campaigned against Yin Yan and pacified Shouyang without harming anyone; the people were grateful and erected a stele to honor him.

sentences.zh: 悛步道從壽陽之鎮，過勔碑，拜敬泣涕。

translations.literal: Quan went on foot from Shouyang to his post; passing Mou's stele, he bowed in reverence and wept.
translations.idiomatic: Quan traveled on foot from Shouyang to take up his post; when he passed his father's stele he bowed in reverence and wept.

sentences.zh: 初，義陽人夏伯宜殺剛陵戍主叛渡淮，虜以爲義陽太守。

translations.literal: Previously, Xia Boyi of Yiyang killed the garrison commander of Gangling, rebelled, crossed the Huai, and the northerners made him Administrator of Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Xia Boyi of Yiyang had killed the garrison commander at Gangling, rebelled, crossed the Huai, and the northern enemies appointed him Administrator of Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 悛設討購誘之，虜△州刺史謝景殺伯宜兄弟、北襄城太守李榮公歸降。

translations.literal: Quan set up pursuit rewards to lure defection; the enemy's Inspector of Si province Xie Jing killed Boyi and his brothers, and Li Rong, Administrator of Northern Xiangcheng, came over and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Quan offered a bounty to induce defection; the enemy's Inspector of Si province, Xie Jing, killed Boyi and his brothers, and Li Rong, Administrator of Northern Xiangcheng, came over and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 悛於州治下立學校，得古禮器銅罍、銅甑、山罍樽、銅豆鍾各二口，獻之。

translations.literal: Quan established a school at the provincial seat, found ancient ritual vessels—two each of bronze lei, bronze zeng, mountain lei zun, and bronze dou bells—and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: At the provincial seat Quan founded a school, discovered ancient ritual vessels—two each of bronze lei, bronze zeng, mountain lei zun, and bronze dou bells—and presented them to the throne.

sentences.zh: 遷長兼侍中。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Senior Concurrent Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Senior Clerk concurrently serving as Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 車駕數幸悛宅。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage often visited Quan's residence.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor often visited Quan's home.

sentences.zh: 宅盛治山池，造甕牖。

translations.literal: The residence had lavishly landscaped hills and pools, and he built a jar-window pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: His home had splendidly laid-out hills and ponds, and he built a rustic jar-window pavilion.

sentences.zh: 世祖著鹿皮冠，被悛菟皮衾，於牖中宴樂，以冠賜悛，至夜乃去。

translations.literal: The Heir Apparent wore a deerskin cap, covered himself with Quan's rabbit-fur quilt, feasted and made merry in the pavilion, bestowed the cap on Quan, and did not leave until night.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu wore a deerskin cap, wrapped himself in Quan's rabbit-fur quilt, and feasted in the pavilion; he gave the cap to Quan and did not leave until nightfall.

sentences.zh: 後悛從駕登蔣山，上數歎曰：「貧賤之交不可忘，糟糠之妻不下堂。

translations.literal: Later Quan accompanied the emperor up Mount Jiang; the emperor sighed repeatedly and said: "Friendship in poverty and low estate must not be forgotten; the wife who shared chaff and husks must not be sent from the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Later Quan accompanied the emperor up Mount Jiang; the emperor sighed again and again and said, "One must not forget friends from humble days, nor cast aside the wife who shared one's coarse fare.

sentences.zh: 」顧謂悛曰：「此況卿也。

translations.literal: " He turned and said to Quan: "This applies to you.
translations.idiomatic: " He turned to Quan and said, "That is your case.

sentences.zh: 世言富貴好改其素情，吾雖有四海，今日與卿盡布衣之適。

translations.literal: People say that wealth and rank love to change one's plain nature; though I possess all within the four seas, today with you I enjoy to the fullest the pleasures of common cloth.
translations.idiomatic: People say wealth and rank change one's true nature; though I rule all within the four seas, today with you I mean to enjoy the ease of commoners to the full.

sentences.zh: 」悛起拜謝。

translations.literal: " Quan rose, bowed, and thanked him.
translations.idiomatic: " Quan rose, bowed, and thanked him.

sentences.zh: 遷冠軍將軍，司徒左長史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to General Who Vanquishes the Foe and Senior Clerk of the Left in the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General Who Vanquishes the Foe and Senior Clerk of the Left on the Minister of Education's staff.

sentences.zh: 尋以本官行北兖州緣淮諸軍事。

translations.literal: Soon, retaining his current title, he acted in military affairs along the Huai in Northern Yan province.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, with his existing rank, he took charge of military affairs along the Huai in Northern Yan province.

sentences.zh: 徙始興王前軍長史、平蠻校尉、蜀郡太守，將軍如故，行益州府、州事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Senior Clerk on the Prince of Shixing's Vanguard Army staff, made Colonel Who Pacifies the Barbarians and Grand Administrator of Shu commandery, his general's title unchanged, acting in the affairs of the Yi prefecture and province.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Senior Clerk on the Prince of Shixing's Vanguard Army staff, made Colonel Who Pacifies the Barbarians and Grand Administrator of Shu commandery, retaining his general's rank while administering the Yi princely establishment and province.

sentences.zh: 郡尋改爲內史。

translations.literal: The commandery was soon changed to an internal governor's post.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery was soon redesignated an internal governorship.

sentences.zh: 隨府轉安西。

translations.literal: Following the princely establishment, he was transferred to Pacification of the West.
translations.idiomatic: When the princely staff moved, he transferred with it to Pacification of the West.

sentences.zh: 悛治事嚴辦，以是會旨。

translations.literal: Quan handled affairs strictly and efficiently, and thereby won approval.
translations.idiomatic: Quan ran affairs with strict efficiency and thereby won the throne's approval.

sentences.zh: 宋代太祖輔政，有意欲鑄錢，以禪讓之際，未及施行。

translations.literal: In Song times, when the Founding Emperor was regent, he intended to cast coinage, but at the juncture of the abdication he had not yet carried it out.
translations.idiomatic: During the Song, when the Founding Emperor was regent he intended to cast new coinage, but at the moment of the abdication he had not yet put the plan into effect.

sentences.zh: ，奉朝請孔覬上鑄錢均貨議，辭證甚博。

translations.literal: Court Attendant Kong Gu submitted a memorial on casting coinage and equalizing currency, with argumentation very extensive.
translations.idiomatic: Court Attendant Kong Gu submitted a memorial entitled "On Casting Coinage and Equalizing Currency," supported by very extensive argument.

sentences.zh: 其略以爲「食貨相通，理勢自然。

translations.literal: Its gist held that "food and currency interflow—the principle and tendency are natural.
translations.idiomatic: Its gist was that "food and currency circulate together by natural principle and tendency.

sentences.zh: 李悝曰『糴甚貴傷民，甚賤傷農』。

translations.literal: Li Kui said: 'When grain is bought at too high a price it harms the people; when too cheap it harms the farmers.'
translations.idiomatic: Li Kui said, 'When grain is bought too dear it harms the people; when too cheap it harms the farmers.'

sentences.zh: 民傷則離散，農傷則國貧。

translations.literal: When the people are harmed they scatter; when farmers are harmed the state grows poor.
translations.idiomatic: When the people suffer they disperse; when farmers suffer the state grows poor.

sentences.zh: 甚賤與甚貴，其傷一也。

translations.literal: Being too cheap and being too expensive do the same harm.
translations.idiomatic: Extremes of cheapness and dearness inflict the same injury.

sentences.zh: 三吳國之關閫，比歲被水潦而糴不貴，是天下錢少，非穀穰賤，此不可不察也。

translations.literal: The Three Wu are the nation's gates; in recent years they have suffered floods yet grain prices are not high—this shows coin in the realm is scarce, not that grain is abundantly cheap; this must not go unexamined.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Wu are the nation's gateway; though flooded in recent years, grain prices have not risen—showing that coin in the realm is scarce, not that harvests are abundant and grain cheap. This cannot be overlooked.

sentences.zh: 鑄錢之弊，在輕重屢變。

translations.literal: The defect of coin casting lies in the weight and value repeatedly changing.
translations.idiomatic: The trouble with coinage lies in the repeated shifting of weight and value.

sentences.zh: 重錢患難用，而難用爲累輕；

translations.literal: Heavy coin worries over difficulty in use, and difficulty in use becomes a burden tending toward lightness;
translations.idiomatic: Heavy coin is hard to use, and difficulty of use drives people toward lighter coin;

sentences.zh: 輕錢弊盜鑄，而盜鑄爲禍深。

translations.literal: light coin has the defect of illicit casting, and illicit casting brings deep calamity.
translations.idiomatic: light coin invites illicit casting, and illicit casting brings deep harm.

sentences.zh: 民所盜鑄，嚴法不禁者，由上鑄錢惜銅愛工也。

translations.literal: What the people illicitly cast strict law cannot stop, because those above who cast coin spare copper and cherish labor.
translations.idiomatic: The reason strict law cannot stop popular illicit casting is that the government, when minting coin, spares copper and labor.

sentences.zh: 惜銅愛工者，謂錢無用之器，以通交易，務欲令輕而數多，使省工而易成，不詳慮其爲患也。

translations.literal: "Spare copper and cherish labor" means treating coin as a useless vessel for facilitating exchange, striving to make it light and numerous, saving labor and making it easy to produce, without carefully considering the harm.
translations.idiomatic: To "spare copper and labor" is to treat coin as a mere tool of exchange, striving to make it light and plentiful, easy and cheap to produce, without fully weighing the harm.

sentences.zh: 自漢鑄五銖錢，至宋文帝，歷五百餘年，制度世有廢興，而不變五銖錢者，明其輕重可法，得貨之宜。

translations.literal: From Han's casting of five-zhu coin to Emperor Wen of Song, spanning more than five hundred years, institutions rose and fell with the ages, yet the five-zhu standard never changed—showing its weight and value could serve as law and suited currency.
translations.idiomatic: From the Han casting of five-zhu coin down to Emperor Wen of Song, more than five hundred years passed; though institutions rose and fell, the five-zhu standard never changed—proof that its weight could serve as law and suited the needs of trade.

sentences.zh: 以爲宜開置泉府，方牧貢金，大興鎔鑄。

translations.literal: He held that it would be fitting to establish a treasury for coin, have regional governors present gold, and greatly expand smelting and casting.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed establishing a coin treasury, requiring regional governors to submit gold, and greatly expanding smelting and minting.

sentences.zh: 錢重五銖，一依漢法。

translations.literal: Coin should weigh five zhu, entirely following Han law.
translations.idiomatic: Coin should weigh five zhu, following Han practice in full.

sentences.zh: 府庫已實，國用有儲，乃量奉祿，薄賦稅，則家給民足。

translations.literal: Once treasuries are full and state expenses have reserves, then regulate stipends and reduce taxes, and households will be supplied and the people sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Once the treasuries are filled and state expenses secured, stipends can be measured out and taxes lightened, and households will be supplied and the people content.

sentences.zh: 頃盜鑄新錢者，皆效作翦鑿，不鑄大錢也。

translations.literal: Recently those who illicitly cast new coin all imitate clipping and chiseling; they do not cast large coin.
translations.idiomatic: Recently illicit minters of new coin simply imitate clipping and carving; they do not cast large pieces.

sentences.zh: 摩澤淄染，始皆類故；

translations.literal: Polishing, dyeing, and soaking—all at first resemble old coin;
translations.idiomatic: Rubbed, dyed, and soaked, they at first look like old coin;

sentences.zh: 交易之後，渝變還新。

translations.literal: after circulation they change color and appear new again.
translations.idiomatic: but after passing in trade their altered color shows them as new again.

sentences.zh: 良民弗皆淄染，不復行矣。

translations.literal: If good citizens do not all dye them, the practice will no longer circulate.
translations.idiomatic: If honest people do not all dye them, the coins will no longer circulate.

sentences.zh: 所鬻賣者，皆徒失其物。

translations.literal: Those who sell them simply lose their goods in vain.
translations.idiomatic: Those who sell them simply lose their goods for nothing.

sentences.zh: 盜鑄者，復賤買新錢，淄染更用，反覆生詐，循環起姦，此明主尤所宜禁而不可長也。

translations.literal: The illicit casters buy new coin cheaply again, dye them for reuse; fraud arises in repetition, wickedness rises in cycles—this an enlightened ruler above all should forbid and must not allow to grow.
translations.idiomatic: Illicit casters then buy new coin cheaply, dye it, and use it again; fraud breeds in repetition and wickedness in cycles—what an enlightened ruler above all should forbid and never allow to spread.

sentences.zh: 若官鑄已布於民，便嚴斷翦鑿，小輕破缺無周郭者，悉不得行，官錢細小者，稱合銖兩，銷以爲大。

translations.literal: If official coin has already been distributed among the people, then strictly forbid clipping and chiseling; small, light, broken, or rimless pieces must none circulate; small official coin, weighed to fit the zhu and liang standard, should be melted down into large pieces.
translations.idiomatic: Once official coin has been issued to the people, clipping and carving must be strictly forbidden; small, light, broken, or rimless pieces must not circulate at all; smaller official coin should be weighed to the zhu and liang standard and melted into larger pieces.

sentences.zh: 利貧良之民，塞姦巧之路。

translations.literal: This benefits poor upright citizens and blocks the path of crafty wickedness.
translations.idiomatic: That would benefit poor honest people and block the road of fraud.

sentences.zh: 錢貨旣均，遠近若一，百姓樂業，市道無爭，衣食滋殖矣。

translations.literal: Once coin and goods are equalized, near and far are as one; the people rejoice in their work, markets and ways are without contention, and food and clothing flourish.
translations.idiomatic: Once coin and goods are equalized, near and far will be as one; the people will take joy in their work, markets will be free of strife, and food and clothing will flourish.

sentences.zh: 」時議者多以錢貨轉少，宜更廣鑄，重其銖兩，以防民姦。

translations.literal: " At the time many in deliberation held that coinage was growing scarcer and casting should be expanded, increasing the zhu and liang weight to guard against popular fraud.
translations.idiomatic: " At the time many in court held that coin was growing scarce, that casting should be expanded, and the zhu and liang weight increased to guard against popular fraud.

sentences.zh: 太祖使諸州郡大市銅炭，會晏駕事寢。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor ordered the various provinces and commanderies to market copper and charcoal on a large scale, but when the emperor suddenly died the matter was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor ordered the provinces and commanderies to buy up copper and charcoal on a large scale, but when he suddenly died the plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 永明八年，悛啓世祖曰：「南廣郡界蒙山下，有城名蒙城，可二頃地，有燒鑪四所，高一丈，廣一丈五尺。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yongming, Quan memorialized Emperor Wu: "Within the bounds of Nanguang commandery, below Mount Meng, there is a city called Meng City, about two qing of land, with four smelting furnaces one zhang high and one zhang five chi wide.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Yongming, Quan memorialized Emperor Wu: "Within Nanguang commandery, below Mount Meng, there is a settlement called Meng City on roughly two qing of land, with four smelting furnaces one zhang high and one zhang five chi wide.

sentences.zh: 從蒙城渡水南百許步，平地掘土深二尺，得銅。

translations.literal: One hundred odd paces south across the water from Meng City, digging two chi deep in flat ground, one obtains copper.
translations.idiomatic: Some hundred paces south across the water from Meng City, copper can be obtained by digging two chi deep in level ground.

sentences.zh: 又有古掘銅坑，深二丈，竝居宅處猶存。

translations.literal: There is also an ancient copper-mining pit two zhang deep, and dwelling sites still remain.
translations.idiomatic: There is also an old copper pit two zhang deep, and the sites of former dwellings still survive.

sentences.zh: 鄧通，南安人，漢文帝賜嚴道縣銅山鑄錢，今蒙山近青衣水南，青衣左側竝是故秦之嚴道地。

translations.literal: Deng Tong, a native of Nan'an, was granted by Emperor Wen of Han the copper mountains of Yandao county to cast coin; now Mount Meng is near the south of the Qingyi River, and to the left of Qingyi is all ancient Qin territory of Yandao.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Tong of Nan'an was granted Yandao county's copper mountains by Emperor Wen of Han to cast coin; Mount Meng now lies near the south bank of the Qingyi River, and the area to Qingyi's left is all the old Qin territory of Yandao.

sentences.zh: 青衣縣又改名漢嘉。

translations.literal: Qingyi county was also renamed Hanjia.
translations.idiomatic: Qingyi county was later renamed Hanjia.

sentences.zh: 且蒙山去南安二百里，案此必是通所鑄。

translations.literal: Moreover Mount Meng is two hundred li from Nan'an; judging by this it must be where Tong cast coin.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Mount Meng is two hundred li from Nan'an; by this evidence it must be where Deng Tong cast coin.

sentences.zh: 近喚蒙山獠出，云『甚可經略』。

translations.literal: Recently summoning the Liao of Mount Meng, they said, 'It can very well be developed.'
translations.idiomatic: I recently summoned the tribal people of Mount Meng, who said, 'It can very well be developed.'

sentences.zh: 此議若立，潤利無極。

translations.literal: If this proposal is adopted, profit without limit.
translations.idiomatic: If this plan is adopted, the profit will be boundless.

sentences.zh: 」幷獻蒙山銅一片，又銅石一片，平州鐵刀一口。

translations.literal: " He also presented a piece of Mount Meng copper, a piece of copper ore, and an iron knife from Ping province.
translations.idiomatic: " He also presented a piece of Mount Meng copper, a piece of copper ore, and an iron knife from Ping province.

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 遣使入蜀鑄錢，得千餘萬，功費多，乃止。

translations.literal: Envoys were sent into Shu to cast coin; they obtained more than ten million, but costs were high, and the effort was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys were sent into Shu to cast coin and produced more than ten million pieces, but costs were too high and the project was halted.

sentences.zh: 悛仍代始興王鑑爲持節、監益寧二州諸軍事、益州刺史，將軍如故。

translations.literal: Quan then replaced Wang Jian, Prince of Shixing, as Bearer of the Staff, Supervisor of Military Affairs in Yi and Ning provinces, and Governor of Yi province, his general's title unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Quan then replaced Wang Jian, Prince of Shixing, as Bearer of the Staff, supervisor of military affairs in Yi and Ning, and Governor of Yi, retaining his rank as general.

sentences.zh: 悛旣藉舊恩，尤能悅附人主，承迎權貴。

translations.literal: Quan, relying on old favor, was especially able to please and attach himself to the sovereign and to court the powerful.
translations.idiomatic: Relying on old favor, Quan was especially skilled at winning the sovereign's attachment and courting the powerful.

sentences.zh: 賔客閨房，供費奢廣。

translations.literal: Guests and inner chambers—expenditure was lavish and extensive.
translations.idiomatic: For guests and private entertainments his spending was lavish.

sentences.zh: 罷廣、司二州，傾資貢獻，家無留儲。

translations.literal: When he left Guang and Si provinces, he poured out his wealth in tribute and gifts, and his household kept no reserves.
translations.idiomatic: When he left Guang and Si provinces he poured out his wealth in tribute and gifts, leaving nothing in store at home.

sentences.zh: 在蜀作金浴盆，餘金物稱是。

translations.literal: In Shu he made a gold bathing basin, and other gold objects in proportion.
translations.idiomatic: In Shu he had a gold bathing basin made, with other gold objects to match.

sentences.zh: 罷任，以本號還都，欲獻之，而世祖晏駕，鬱林新立，悛奉獻減少，鬱林知之，諷有司收悛付廷尉，將加誅戮。

translations.literal: When his term ended he returned to the capital with his former title, intending to present the gifts, but Emperor Wu suddenly died and Emperor Yulin had just acceded; Quan reduced his presentation, Yulin learned of it, hinted that officials should arrest Quan and hand him to the Court of Justice, intending execution.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he returned to the capital with his former rank, intending to present the gifts, but Emperor Wu suddenly died and Emperor Yulin had just acceded; Quan scaled back his tribute, and when Yulin learned of it he hinted that officials should arrest Quan and hand him to the Court of Justice for execution.

sentences.zh: 高宗啓救之，見原，禁錮終身。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming of Qi interceded to save him; he was pardoned but imprisoned for life.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming of Qi interceded to save him; he was pardoned but confined for life.

sentences.zh: 雖見廢黜，而賔客日至。

translations.literal: Though disgraced and dismissed, guests came every day.
translations.idiomatic: Though disgraced and dismissed, guests came every day.

sentences.zh: 悛婦弟王法顯同宋桂陽事，遂啓別居，終身不復見之。

translations.literal: Quan's wife's younger brother Wang Faxian was implicated in the Song Guiyang affair; Quan therefore announced separate residence and never saw him again for the rest of his life.
translations.idiomatic: Quan's wife's younger brother Wang Faxian was implicated in the Song Guiyang affair; Quan announced they would live apart and never saw him again for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 海陵王卽位，以白衣除兼左民尚書，尋除正。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Hailing acceded, Quan was appointed from commoner status as Concurrent Minister of the Left Bureau for the People, soon made regular.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Hailing acceded, Quan was appointed from private life as Concurrent Minister of the Left Bureau for the People and soon made regular minister.

sentences.zh: 高宗立，加領驍騎將軍，復故官，駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming of Qi acceded, he was additionally made General of Valiant Cavalry, restored to his former offices, and made Commandant of the Horse Fleet for the Imperial Son-in-Law.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming of Qi acceded, Quan was additionally made General of Valiant Cavalry, restored to his former posts, and again made Commandant of the Horse Fleet for the Imperial Son-in-Law.

sentences.zh: ，虜主侵壽陽，詔悛以本官假節出鎮漅湖，遷散騎常侍、右衞將軍。

translations.literal: When the northern ruler invaded Shouyang, an edict ordered Quan, with his current title and provisional staff, out to garrison Chaohu; he was promoted to Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry and General of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When the northern ruler invaded Shouyang, an edict ordered Quan, with his current rank and provisional staff, out to garrison Chaohu; he was promoted to Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry and General of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 虜寇旣盛，悛又以本官出屯新亭。

translations.literal: As northern incursions grew fierce, Quan again went out with his current title and encamped at Xinting.
translations.idiomatic: As northern raids grew fierce, Quan again went out with his existing rank and encamped at Xinting.

sentences.zh: 悛歷朝皆見恩遇。

translations.literal: Through successive reigns Quan was always treated with favor.
translations.idiomatic: Through successive reigns Quan always enjoyed imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 太祖爲鄱陽王鏘納悛妹爲妃，高宗又爲晉安王寶義納悛女爲妃，自此連姻帝室。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor married Quan's younger sister to Prince Qiang of Poyang; Emperor Ming of Qi married Quan's daughter to Prince Baoyi of Jin'an; from this the family was joined by marriage to the imperial house.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor took Quan's younger sister as consort for Prince Qiang of Poyang; Emperor Ming of Qi took Quan's daughter as consort for Prince Baoyi of Jin'an; from then on the family was linked by marriage to the imperial house.

sentences.zh: 王敬則反，悛出守琅邪城，轉五兵尚書，領太子左衞率。

translations.literal: When Wang Jingze rebelled, Quan went out to hold Langye city, was transferred to Minister of the Five Weapons, and concurrently Commander of the Heir Apparent's Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Jingze rebelled, Quan went out to hold Langye city, was transferred to Minister of the Five Weapons, and concurrently made Commander of the Heir Apparent's Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 未拜，明帝崩，東昏卽位，改授散騎常侍，領驍騎將軍，尚書如故。

translations.literal: Before he took up the post, Emperor Ming died and Emperor Donghun acceded; he was reassigned as Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry, concurrently General of Valiant Cavalry, Minister unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up the post, Emperor Ming of Qi died and Emperor Donghun acceded; he was reassigned Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry, concurrently General of Valiant Cavalry, while retaining his ministry.

sentences.zh: 衞送山陵，卒，年六十一。

translations.literal: Escorting the imperial tomb, he died at age sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: While escorting the imperial tomb he died, aged sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 贈太常，常侍、都尉如故。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Grand Commandant of Ceremonial; Attendant-in-Ordinary and Commandant unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Commandant of Ceremonial; his posts as Attendant-in-Ordinary and Commandant were unchanged.

sentences.zh: 諡曰敬。

translations.literal: His posthumous name was Jing.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous name was Respectful.

sentences.zh: 虞悰

translations.literal: Yu Cong
translations.idiomatic: Yu Cong

sentences.zh: 虞悰字景豫，會稽餘姚人也。

translations.literal: Yu Cong, styled Jingyu, was a native of Yuyao in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Cong, styled Jingyu, was a man of Yuyao in Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 祖嘯父，晉左民尚書。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xiaofu was Jin Minister of the Left Bureau for the People.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xiaofu had been Jin Minister of the Left Bureau for the People.

sentences.zh: 父秀之，黃門郎。

translations.literal: His father Xiuzhi was Gentleman at the Yellow Gates.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xiuzhi had served as Gentleman at the Yellow Gates.

sentences.zh: 悰少而謹敕，有至性。

translations.literal: Cong from youth was careful and restrained, with utmost filial nature.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Cong was careful and disciplined, with deep filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 秀之於都亡，悰東出奔喪，水漿不入口。

translations.literal: When Xiuzhi died in the capital, Cong traveled east to attend the funeral and took no water or food.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiuzhi died in the capital, Cong traveled east to mourn and took neither food nor drink.

sentences.zh: 州辟主簿，建平王參軍，尚書儀曹郎，太子洗馬，領軍長史，正員郎，累至州治中，別駕，黃門郎。

translations.literal: The province recruited him as Chief Clerk; he served as staff officer on the Prince of Jianping's staff, Director in the Ministry of Rites, Groom of the Heir Apparent, Senior Clerk on the Defender's staff, Regular Director, rose through Provincial Controller and Administrative Aide to Gentleman at the Yellow Gates.
translations.idiomatic: The province recruited him as Chief Clerk; he served as staff officer on the Prince of Jianping's staff, Director in the Ministry of Rites, Groom of the Heir Apparent, Senior Clerk on the Defender's staff, Regular Director, and rose through Provincial Controller and Administrative Aide to Gentleman at the Yellow Gates.

sentences.zh: 初，世祖始從官，家尚貧薄，悰推國士之眷，數相分與，每行，必呼上同載，上甚德之。

translations.literal: At first, when the future Emperor Wu first entered official service, his family was still poor; Cong, treating him with the affection due a national stalwart, often shared things with him; whenever he traveled he always called the future emperor to ride together, and the emperor was deeply grateful.
translations.idiomatic: At first, when the future Emperor Wu was just entering official life, his family was still poor; Cong treated him with the affection due a true friend of the realm, often sharing what he had with him; whenever he traveled he always called the future emperor to ride with him, and the emperor was deeply grateful.

sentences.zh: 昇明中，世祖爲中軍，引悰爲諮議參軍，遣吏部郎江謐持手書謂悰曰：「今因江吏郎有白，以君情顧，意欲相屈。

translations.literal: In the Shengming era, when the future Emperor Wu was Central Army commander, he recruited Cong as advisory staff officer and sent Director of the Ministry of Personnel Jiang Mi with a personal letter saying: "Now by way of Director Jiang's report, considering your affectionate regard, I wish to invite you to serve.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shengming era, when the future Emperor Wu commanded the Central Army, he recruited Cong as advisory staff officer and sent Director of the Ministry of Personnel Jiang Mi with a personal letter saying, "On Director Jiang's report, and mindful of your old regard, I wish to ask you to serve.

sentences.zh: 」建元初，轉太子中庶子，遷後軍長史，領步兵校尉，鎮北長史、寧朔將軍、南東海太守。

translations.literal: " At the beginning of Jianyuan he was transferred to Household Subordinate of the Heir Apparent, promoted to Senior Clerk on the Rear Army staff, concurrently Colonel of Footsoldiers, Senior Clerk on the Pacification of the North staff, General of Pacifying the North, and Administrator of Southern Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: " At the beginning of Jianyuan he was transferred to Household Subordinate of the Heir Apparent, promoted to Senior Clerk on the Rear Army staff, concurrently Colonel of Footsoldiers, Senior Clerk on the Pacification of the North staff, General of Pacifying the North, and Administrator of Southern Donghai.

sentences.zh: 尋爲豫章內史，將軍如故。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Internal Governor of Yuzhang, his general's title unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Internal Governor of Yuzhang, retaining his general's rank.

sentences.zh: 悰治家富殖，奴婢無游手，雖在南土，而會稽海味無不畢致焉。

translations.literal: Cong managed his household to great wealth; among servants and maids there were none idle; though in the south he had every sort of Kuaiji seafood delivered without exception.
translations.idiomatic: Cong ran his household to great wealth; among servants and maids none were idle; though he lived in the south, every sort of Kuaiji seafood was always supplied.

sentences.zh: 遷輔國將軍、始興王長史、平蠻校尉、蜀郡太守。

translations.literal: He was promoted to General Who Supports the State, Senior Clerk on the Prince of Shixing's staff, Colonel Who Pacifies the Barbarians, and Grand Administrator of Shu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General Who Supports the State, Senior Clerk on the Prince of Shixing's staff, Colonel Who Pacifies the Barbarians, and Grand Administrator of Shu commandery.

sentences.zh: 轉司徒司馬，將軍如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Army Supervisor of the Department of State Affairs, his general's title unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Army Supervisor of the Department of State Affairs, retaining his general's rank.

sentences.zh: 悰善爲滋味，和齊皆有方法。

translations.literal: Cong was skilled at flavors; blending and seasoning all had method.
translations.idiomatic: Cong was skilled in flavor; his blending and seasoning all had method.

sentences.zh: 豫章王嶷盛饌享賔，謂悰曰：「今日肴羞，寧有所遺不？

translations.literal: Prince Yi of Yuzhang held a lavish feast for guests and said to Cong: "Today's delicacies—is anything lacking?
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yi of Yuzhang held a lavish feast for guests and said to Cong, "Of today's dishes, is anything missing?

sentences.zh: 」悰曰：「恨無黃頷臛，何曾《食疏》所載也。

translations.literal: " Cong said: "I regret there is no yellow-jaw stew—the dish recorded in He Zeng's 《Food Notes》.
translations.idiomatic: " Cong said, "Only yellow-jaw stew is missing—the dish recorded in He Zeng's 《Food Notes》.

sentences.zh: 」遷散騎常侍，太子右率。

translations.literal: " He was promoted to Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry and Commander of the Heir Apparent's Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: " He was promoted to Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry and Commander of the Heir Apparent's Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 永明八年，大水，百官戎服救太廟，悰朱衣乘車鹵簿，於宣陽門外行馬內驅打人，爲有司所奏，見原。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yongming, during great floods, all officials wore military dress to rescue the Imperial Ancestral Temple; Cong, in vermilion robes with carriage escort, drove people within the riding grounds at Xuanyang Gate; he was impeached by the responsible officials and pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Yongming, during severe floods, all officials wore military dress to aid the Imperial Ancestral Temple; Cong, in vermilion robes with full escort, drove people within the riding grounds at Xuanyang Gate; the responsible officials impeached him, and he was pardoned.

sentences.zh: 上以悰布衣之舊，從容謂悰曰：「我當令卿復祖業。

translations.literal: The emperor, considering Cong an old friend from common cloth days, said at ease: "I shall have you restore your grandfather's career.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, mindful of their old friendship from commoner days, said easily to Cong, "I shall have you restore your grandfather's career.

sentences.zh: 」轉侍中，朝廷咸驚其美拜。

translations.literal: " He was transferred to Attendant-in-Ordinary, and the court all marveled at this splendid appointment.
translations.idiomatic: " He was transferred to Attendant-in-Ordinary, and the whole court marveled at so fine an appointment.

sentences.zh: 遷祠部尚書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of the Imperial Ancestral Temples.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Minister of the Imperial Ancestral Temples.

sentences.zh: 世祖幸芳林園，就悰求扁米。

translations.literal: The emperor visited the Fragrant Grove Park and asked Cong for polished rice.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu visited the Fragrant Grove Park and asked Cong for polished rice.

sentences.zh: 悰獻及雜肴數十轝，太官鼎味不及也。

translations.literal: Cong presented it along with several dozen cartloads of assorted delicacies, which the Imperial Kitchen's cauldron dishes could not match.
translations.idiomatic: Cong sent it along with dozens of cartloads of assorted delicacies that outshone even the Imperial Kitchen's finest dishes.

sentences.zh: 上就悰求諸飲食方，悰秘不肯出，上醉後體不快，悰乃獻醒酒鯖鮓一方而已。

translations.literal: The emperor asked Cong for his various recipes for food and drink; Cong kept them secret and would not produce them. After the emperor drank himself ill and felt unwell, Cong then presented only one recipe for sobering pickled mackerel.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Cong for his culinary recipes, but Cong kept them secret. When the emperor drank too much and felt ill, Cong offered only a single recipe for hangover-curing pickled mackerel.

sentences.zh: 出爲冠軍將軍，車騎長史，轉度支尚書，領步兵校尉。

translations.literal: He went out as General Who Vanquishes the Foe and Senior Clerk on the Chariots and Cavalry staff, was transferred to Minister of Revenue, and concurrently served as Colonel of Footsoldiers.
translations.idiomatic: He left court as General Who Vanquishes the Foe and Senior Clerk on the Chariots and Cavalry staff, was made Minister of Revenue, and concurrently commanded the Footsoldiers.

sentences.zh: 鬱林立，改領右軍將軍，揚州大中正，兼大匠卿。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yulin acceded he was changed to lead the Right Army as general, became Chief Rectifier of Yang province, and concurrently served as Director of the Imperial Workshops.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yulin came to the throne, Cong was changed to command the Right Army, made Chief Rectifier of Yang province, and concurrently Director of the Imperial Workshops.

sentences.zh: 起休安陵，於陵所受局下牛酒，坐免官。

translations.literal: He oversaw construction of the Xiuan Mausoleum and, for oxen and wine received from subordinates at the tomb site, was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: He supervised construction of the Xiuan Mausoleum and was dismissed for accepting oxen and wine from subordinates at the tomb works.

sentences.zh: 隆昌元年，以白衣領職。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longchang he held his post in plain clothes.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Longchang he resumed his duties in plain clothes.

sentences.zh: 鬱林廢，悰竊歎曰：「王、徐遂縛袴廢天子，天下豈有此理邪？

translations.literal: When Emperor Yulin was deposed, Cong sighed privately, saying: "Wang and Xu have actually trussed up their trousers and deposed the Son of Heaven—can there be such a principle under heaven?"
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yulin was deposed, Cong sighed to himself: "Wang and Xu have actually bound up their trousers and deposed the Son of Heaven—has the world ever known such a thing?"

sentences.zh: 」廷興元年，復領右軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yanxing he again led the Right Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yanxing he again commanded the Right Army.

sentences.zh: 明帝立，悰稱疾不陪位。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming acceded, Cong claimed illness and did not take his place at the ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming of Qi came to the throne, Cong pleaded illness and did not attend the enthronement.

sentences.zh: 帝使尚書令王晏賫廢立事示悰，以悰舊人，引參佐命。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Minister of Education Wang Yan to present the account of deposition and enthronement to Cong and, because Cong was an old associate, drew him in to assist in establishing the new order.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Minister of Education Wang Yan to show Cong the record of the deposition and enthronement and, as an old associate, sought to draw him into assisting the new regime.

sentences.zh: 悰謂晏曰：「主上聖明，公卿戮力，寧假朽老以匡贊惟新乎？

translations.literal: Cong said to Yan: "Our lord is sage and enlightened; the nobles and ministers exert themselves together—how could one borrow a decayed old man to help support renewal?"
translations.idiomatic: Cong said to Yan: "Our lord is sage and enlightened, and the nobles and ministers are all doing their part—why borrow a worn-out old man to help usher in the new order?"

sentences.zh: 不敢聞命。

translations.literal: I dare not accept the command."
translations.idiomatic: I dare not accept such a commission."

sentences.zh: 」朝議欲糾之，僕射徐孝嗣曰：「此亦古之遺直。

translations.literal: "Court deliberation wished to impeach him, but the Left Deputy Director Xu Xiaosi said: "This too is an upright remnant of antiquity."
translations.idiomatic: "The court wished to impeach him, but Vice Director Xu Xiaosi said: "This is also the sort of blunt integrity the ancients prized."

sentences.zh: 」衆議乃止。

translations.literal: "The assembly's deliberation then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: "The assembly then dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 悰稱疾篤還東，上表曰：「臣族陋海區，身微稽土，猥屬興運，荷竊稠私，徒越星紀，終慚報答。

translations.literal: Cong claimed grave illness and returned east, memorializing: "Your servant's clan is humble in this coastal region; my person is slight upon the soil of Kuaiji. I have undeservedly met a rising fortune and borne thick private favor, yet have only crossed a twelve-year cycle and remain ashamed at repayment.
translations.idiomatic: Cong claimed serious illness and returned east, memorializing: "Your servant's clan is humble in this coastal region; I am a slight man of Kuaiji. I have undeservedly lived in a time of rising fortune and received thick private favor, yet have only passed one twelve-year cycle and remain ashamed that I cannot repay it.

sentences.zh: 衞養乖方，抱疾嬰固，寢瘵以來，倏踰旬朔，頻加醫治，曾未瘳損。

translations.literal: Nursing and care have gone against the proper method; I bear illness wrapped in obstinacy. Since this wasting sickness began, it has suddenly passed more than a month; though physicians have been applied repeatedly, there has been no recovery or improvement.
translations.idiomatic: My care has gone wrong, and I am gripped by stubborn illness. Since this wasting sickness began, more than a month has suddenly passed; though physicians have treated me repeatedly, I have not improved.

sentences.zh: 惟此朽頓，理難振復，乞解所職，盡療餘辰。

translations.literal: Only this decayed exhaustion, by reason hard to revive and restore—I beg to be released from my posts and to spend my remaining time wholly in healing.
translations.idiomatic: This exhausted frame can hardly be restored; I beg to be released from my offices and to spend what time remains wholly in recuperation.

sentences.zh: 」詔賜假百日。

translations.literal: "An edict granted him leave for one hundred days.
translations.idiomatic: "An edict granted him one hundred days' leave.

sentences.zh: 轉給事中，光祿大夫，尋加正員常侍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Supervising Attendant, Grand Master for the Palace, and soon additionally made Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Supervising Attendant and Grand Master for the Palace, and soon made Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary.

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 時年六十五。

translations.literal: He was then sixty-five years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was sixty-five years old.

sentences.zh: 悰性敦實，與人知識，必相存訪，親疏皆有終始，世以此稱之。

translations.literal: Cong's nature was sincere and solid; with anyone he came to know he always paid mutual visits, and whether close or distant all had proper beginnings and ends—his age praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Cong was sincere and steadfast; with everyone he knew he kept up mutual visits, treating kin and strangers alike with constancy from first to last, and the age praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 從弟袤，矢志不仕。

translations.literal: His cousin Mao vowed never to take office.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Mao had vowed never to enter official service.

sentences.zh: 王敬則反，取袤監會稽郡，而軍事悉付寒人張靈寶，郡人攻郡殺靈寶，袤以不豫事得全。

translations.literal: When Wang Jingze rebelled he took Mao to oversee Kuaiji commandery, but military affairs were all entrusted to the commoner Zhang Lingbao; the people of the commandery attacked the prefecture and killed Lingbao, and Mao was spared because he had not been involved in the affair.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Jingze rebelled he put Mao in charge of Kuaiji commandery, but entrusted all military affairs to the commoner Zhang Lingbao; the people of the commandery stormed the prefecture and killed Lingbao, and Mao was spared because he had taken no part in the matter.

sentences.zh: 胡諧之

translations.literal: Hu Xiezhi
