translations.idiomatic: Hu Xiezhi

sentences.zh: 胡諧之，豫章南昌人也。

translations.literal: Hu Xiezhi was a native of Nanchang in Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Xiezhi was a man of Nanchang in Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 祖廉之，治書侍御史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Lianzhi was Attending Secretary in the Office for Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Lianzhi had been Attending Secretary in the Office for Punishments.

sentences.zh: 父翼之，州辟不就。

translations.literal: His father Yizhi was recruited by the province but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yizhi was recruited by the province but declined to serve.

sentences.zh: 諧之初辟州從事主簿，臨賀王國常侍，員外郎，撫軍行參軍，晉熙王安西中兵參軍，南梁郡太守。

translations.literal: Xiezhi at first was recruited as Chief Clerk of the provincial aides, Constant Attendant in the Kingdom of Linhe, External Clerk, acting staff officer on the Pacification Army staff, central army staff officer on the Prince of Jinxi's Army That Guards the West staff, and Grand Administrator of Nanliang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Xiezhi was first recruited as Chief Clerk of the provincial aides, then served as Constant Attendant in the Kingdom of Linhe, External Clerk, acting staff officer on the Pacification Army staff, central army staff officer on the Prince of Jinxi's Army That Guards the West staff, and Grand Administrator of Nanliang commandery.

sentences.zh: 以器局見稱。

translations.literal: He was praised for his capacity and breadth of view.
translations.idiomatic: He was praised for his talent and breadth of vision.

sentences.zh: 徙邵陵王南中郎中兵，領汝南太守，不拜。

translations.literal: He was transferred to central army officer on the Prince of Shaoling's Southern Gentlemen-in-Attendance staff and concurrently Grand Administrator of Runan, but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to central army officer on the Prince of Shaoling's Southern Gentlemen-in-Attendance staff and concurrently Grand Administrator of Runan, but declined the appointment.

sentences.zh: 除射聲校尉，州別駕。

translations.literal: He was appointed Colonel of the Archers and Administrative Aide of the province.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Colonel of the Archers and Administrative Aide of the province.

sentences.zh: 除左軍將軍，不拜。

translations.literal: He was appointed General of the Left Army but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed General of the Left Army but declined.

sentences.zh: 仍除邵陵王左軍諮議。

translations.literal: He was then appointed advisory officer on the Prince of Shaoling's Left Army staff.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed advisory officer on the Prince of Shaoling's Left Army staff.

sentences.zh: 世祖頓盆城，使諧之守尋陽城，及爲江州，復以諧之爲別駕，委以事任。

translations.literal: When the Heir Apparent was stationed at Pencheng he had Xiezhi guard Xunyang city; when he became governor of Jiang province he again made Xiezhi Administrative Aide and entrusted him with affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the future Emperor Wu was stationed at Pencheng he had Xiezhi guard Xunyang; when he became governor of Jiang province he again made Xiezhi Administrative Aide and entrusted him with full responsibility.

sentences.zh: 文惠太子鎮襄陽，世祖以諧之心腹，出爲北中郎征虜司馬、扶風太守，爵關內侯。

translations.literal: When Crown Prince Wenhui was stationed at Xiangyang, the Heir Apparent, because Xiezhi was a trusted confidant, sent him out as Major on the Northern Gentlemen-in-Attendance Punitive Campaign against the Barbarians staff and Grand Administrator of Fufeng, with the title Marquis within the Passes.
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Wenhui was stationed at Xiangyang, the future Emperor Wu sent his trusted confidant Xiezhi out as Major on the Northern Gentlemen-in-Attendance Punitive Campaign staff and Grand Administrator of Fufeng, ennobling him as Marquis within the Passes.

sentences.zh: 在鎮毗贊，甚有心力。

translations.literal: At his post he assisted and supported diligently and with great devoted effort.
translations.idiomatic: At his post he assisted with great energy and devotion.

sentences.zh: ，還爲給事中，驍騎將軍，本州中正，轉黃門郎，領羽林監。

translations.literal: He returned and became Supervising Attendant, General of Valiant Cavalry, Rectifier of his home province, was transferred to Gentleman at the Yellow Gates, and led the Forest of Feathers Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to court as Supervising Attendant and General of Valiant Cavalry, served as Rectifier of his home province, was transferred to Gentleman at the Yellow Gates, and commanded the Forest of Feathers Guard.

sentences.zh: ，轉守衞尉，中正如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Defender of the Minister of the Guards, his rectifier post unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Defender of the Minister of the Guards while retaining his post as Rectifier.

sentences.zh: 明年，加給事中。

translations.literal: The next year he was additionally made Supervising Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was additionally made Supervising Attendant.

sentences.zh: 三年，遷散騎常侍，太子右率。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to Attendant-in-Ordinary and Leader of the Right for the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was transferred to Attendant-in-Ordinary and Leader of the Right for the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 五年，遷左衞將軍，加給事中，中正如故。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to General of the Left Guard, additionally made Supervising Attendant, his rectifier post unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was transferred to General of the Left Guard, additionally made Supervising Attendant, and retained his post as Rectifier.

sentences.zh: 諧之風形瓌潤，善自居處，兼以舊恩見遇，朝士多與交遊。

translations.literal: Xiezhi's bearing was striking and lustrous; he was skilled in deportment, and because of old favor he was well received—many court gentlemen associated with him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiezhi was striking in appearance and graceful in bearing; because of old favor he was well received at court, and many officials sought his company.

sentences.zh: 六年，遷都官尚書。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was transferred to Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 上欲遷諧之，嘗從容謂諧之曰：「江州有幾侍中邪？

translations.literal: The emperor wished to transfer Xiezhi and once said to him at ease: "How many Attendants-in-Ordinary does Jiang province have?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to promote Xiezhi and once asked him casually: "How many Attendants-in-Ordinary does Jiang province have?"

sentences.zh: 」諧之答曰：「近世唯有程道惠一人而已。

translations.literal: Xiezhi answered: "In recent times there has been only Cheng Daohui alone."
translations.idiomatic: Xiezhi answered: "In recent times there has been only Cheng Daohui."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「當令有二。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "We shall make it two."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "We shall make it two."

sentences.zh: 」後以語尚書令王儉，儉意更異，乃以爲太子中庶子，領左衞率。

translations.literal: Later he told this to Minister of Education Wang Jian; Jian's view differed, and so Xiezhi was made Household Subordinate of the Heir Apparent and Leader of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Later he told Minister of Education Wang Jian, whose view differed; Xiezhi was therefore made Household Subordinate of the Heir Apparent and Leader of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 諧之兄謨之亡，諧之上表曰：「臣私門罪釁，早備荼苦。

translations.literal: When Xiezhi's elder brother Mozhi died, Xiezhi memorialized: "Your servant's private household has sins and offenses and long ago tasted bitterness.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiezhi's elder brother Mozhi died, he memorialized: "Your servant's family has long known guilt and bitterness.

sentences.zh: 兄弟三人，共相撫鞠，嬰孩抱疾，得及成人。

translations.literal: Three brothers together nurtured and raised one another; as infants we bore illness yet reached adulthood.
translations.idiomatic: We three brothers raised one another; though sickly as infants, we all reached adulthood.

sentences.zh: 長兄臣諶之，復早殞沒，與亡第二兄臣謨之銜戚家庭，得蒙訓長，情同極廕。

translations.literal: The eldest brother, your servant Chenzhi, again died early; with the deceased second brother, your servant Mozhi, we shared grief in the family, received training and growth, and our affection was like that of the most sheltered shade.
translations.idiomatic: My eldest brother Chenzhi also died young; my late second brother Mozhi and I shared our family's grief, were raised and taught together, and loved one another as deeply as kin could.

sentences.zh: 何圖一旦奄見棄放，吉凶分違，不獲臨奉，乞解所職。

translations.literal: Who could have thought that in a single day he would suddenly be cast away; fortune and misfortune are sundered, and I cannot attend and serve—I beg to be released from my posts.
translations.idiomatic: Who could have imagined he would suddenly be taken from us? Fortune and misfortune are now divided, and I cannot attend his rites—I beg to be released from my offices.

sentences.zh: 」詔不許。

translations.literal: An edict did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict refused his request.

sentences.zh: 改衞尉，中庶子如故。

translations.literal: He was changed to Defender of the Minister of the Guards, his subordinate post unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Defender of the Minister of the Guards while retaining his post as Household Subordinate.

sentences.zh: 八年，上遣諧之率禁兵討巴東王子響於江陵，兼長史行事。

translations.literal: In the eighth year the emperor sent Xiezhi to lead the palace guard troops to campaign against Prince Zixiang of Badong at Jiangling, concurrently acting as Senior Clerk in charge of affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year the emperor sent Xiezhi to lead the palace guard against Prince Zixiang of Badong at Jiangling, concurrently acting Senior Clerk in charge of affairs.

sentences.zh: 臺軍爲子響所敗，有司奏免官，權行軍事如故。

translations.literal: The imperial army was defeated by Zixiang; the relevant offices memorialized to dismiss him from office, but he was provisionally allowed to conduct military affairs as before.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial army was defeated by Zixiang; the authorities memorialized for his dismissal, but he was allowed to conduct military affairs provisionally as before.

sentences.zh: 復爲衞尉，領中庶子，本州中正。

translations.literal: He again became Defender of the Minister of the Guards, led the Household Subordinate post, and served as Rectifier of his home province.
translations.idiomatic: He again became Defender of the Minister of the Guards, concurrently Household Subordinate, and Rectifier of his home province.

sentences.zh: 諧之有識計，每朝廷官缺及應遷代，密量上所用人，皆如其言，虞悰以此稱服之。

translations.literal: Xiezhi had discernment and stratagem; whenever court offices were vacant or due for transfer and replacement, he secretly gauged whom the emperor would use, and in every case it was as he said—Yu Cong for this reason praised and admired him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiezhi was shrewd and resourceful; whenever a court office fell vacant or was due for rotation, he would quietly predict whom the emperor would appoint, and he was always right—Yu Cong admired him greatly for this.

sentences.zh: 十年，轉度支尚書，領衞尉。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was transferred to Minister of Revenue and led the Minister of the Guards.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was transferred to Minister of Revenue and concurrently Defender of the Minister of the Guards.

sentences.zh: 明年，卒，年五十一。

translations.literal: The next year he died at age fifty-one.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he died at the age of fifty-one.

sentences.zh: 贈右將軍、豫州刺史。

translations.literal: He was posthumously awarded General of the Right and Inspector of Yu province.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made General of the Right and Inspector of Yu province.

sentences.zh: 諡曰肅。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Su.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous epithet was Su.

translations.literal: Appraisal
translations.idiomatic: Appraisal

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：送錢贏兩，言此無忘，一笥之懷，報以都尉，千金可失，貴在人心。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Sending money and winning two—speak of this and do not forget; the feeling in one basket is repaid with the Commandant of the Chariots; a thousand in gold may be lost, but what is precious lies in the human heart.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer says: Gifts of money and games of chance—speak of these and do not forget them; a single basket of goodwill may be repaid with the rank of Commandant of the Chariots; a thousand in gold may be lost, but what matters is the human heart.

sentences.zh: 夫謹而信，汎愛衆，其爲利也博矣。

translations.literal: To be careful and trustworthy, to love broadly the multitude—the profit in this is vast.
translations.idiomatic: To be careful and trustworthy, and to love the many broadly—how vast the profit in that is.

sentences.zh: 況乎先覺潛龍，結厚於布素，隨才致位，理固然也。

translations.literal: How much more when one who foresaw while still a hidden dragon formed deep ties in plain cloth, and according to talent attained rank—this is reason's natural course.
translations.idiomatic: How much more when those who discerned merit in a prince still unrisen formed deep ties in humble days, and were placed in office according to their talents—this is only as reason would have it.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：到藉豪華，晚懷虛素。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Dao relied on magnificence, yet in later years cherished plain simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium says: Dao drew on grandeur, yet in his later years embraced plain simplicity.

sentences.zh: 虞生富厚，侈不違度。

translations.literal: Yu Cong was born rich and ample, extravagant yet not beyond measure.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Cong was born to wealth, lavish yet never beyond propriety.

sentences.zh: 劉實朝交，胡乃蕃故，頡頏亮采，康衢騁步。

translations.literal: Liu was solid in court friendship; Hu was an old associate from the frontier; each matched bright talent and strode the broad highway.
translations.idiomatic: Liu was steadfast in court friendship; Hu was an old companion from the frontier; each matched bright talent and walked the open road at ease.
